exposure: Mode of delivery (Cesarean section or vaginal delivery)
outcome: Neonatal near miss (infants who nearly died but survived from birth to 28 days)
cohort: 403 neonates admitted to neonatal intensive care units of hospitals in East Wollega, West Ethiopia, between July 15 and August 30, 2019
finding: The study found a high rate of neonatal near miss (48.60%) and identified maternal residence in a rural area, Cesarean section delivery, referral status, female sex of the neonate, and multiple births as significant risk factors.
mod_finding: Cesarean section delivery was significantly associated with neonatal near miss (adjusted odds ratio = 10.68, 95% confidence interval = (2.95, 38.71)).
